statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail holds the watch floor at 20% while Stress eases to 78% inside the high band as the long-end yield selloff stalls.
recommendation: Tail stays at the watch floor because the overnight NQ path remains two-sided inside an unchanged narrow band, the marginal new high was rejected and the rates amplifier has stabilised with the 10-year flat at 5.240%. Stress remains high on long-end yields near 24-year peaks, a dollar at 17-month highs, a residual Gulf conflict premium in energy, a broadly weaker Asian session and the September payrolls release at 12:30Z. The flagged window stays narrow, spanning 12:30Z to 15:00Z around the release and the U.S. cash open.
headline: NQ holds an unchanged overnight band as the long-end yield selloff stalls into the September payrolls print
body: NQ futures trade 30,874.25 (+0.37%) as of 06:15Z, still inside an overnight range of 30,760.25-30,934.75 that has not widened over the past hour. Price sits about 60 points below the high after the marginal new extreme was rejected, inside a band roughly 0.57% wide, so the structure is two-sided rather than persistently directional and no repeated extension after failed retracements is observed. Cash NDX closed 30,501.56 (+0.31%) on October 1 with a 30,274.65-30,616.24 range against a 52-week high of 30,770.63, and VIX finished at 16.39. The most important change from the previous hours is that the rates amplifier has stalled. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.240% against a 5.238% prior close in a narrow 5.231-5.262 session band, well below Thursday's 5.34% peak, which was the highest since 2002 after the steepest quarterly rise in 32 years; the 2-year sits near 4.7934% after falling 10 basis points overnight on dovish Fed commentary, and the Federal Reserve H.15 release for September 30 shows 10-year 5.29% and 2-year 4.88%. Oil is also easing, with WTI at 92.13 (-0.79%) and Brent at 101.65 (-0.57%) after Brent settled above 102 on Thursday, so the Gulf conflict premium tied to a reported third U.S. carrier deployment is being partly unwound rather than extended. The dollar remains the firmest cross-asset signal: the dollar index is near 102, its highest since April 2025, with the euro at 1.1250 after an 0.8% overnight fall to its lowest since May 2025 and the yen at 157.8. Asia is broadly lower, with MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan down 0.3%, the Nikkei 225 off 1.1%, and the Hang Seng down 2.6% on its return from holiday, while mainland China is closed for Golden Week and India is also shut. Tokyo core CPI at 2.7%, the fastest in 10 months, strengthens the Bank of Japan tightening case. U.S. cash closed higher on Thursday for a second session led by semiconductors after Micron beat and raised guidance, and the September ISM Manufacturing PMI printed 54.5% with a prices index of 77.9%, up 6.8 points, which keeps the inflation side of the rates story active. The dominant mode stays mixed: a firm NQ against weak Asian equities, a strong dollar and high yields is cross-asset conflict rather than aligned amplification, and under this contract conflicting signals raise Stress more than Tail. September payrolls land at 12:30Z with consensus near 90,000 jobs and an unchanged 4.1% unemployment rate, followed by August Factory Orders at 14:00Z. The release is a checkpoint, not an automatic block: before it prints, hypothetical post-event alignment is not treated as observed, so the flagged window is kept narrow at 12:30Z to 15:00Z and the conditional forecast reaches the block threshold only for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots covering the cash open and the delayed second leg.

lookbackSummary: The previous 24 published Claude hours stayed inside the watch band apart from one orange hour at 06:00Z on October 1, when Tail touched 25% on a brief trend-up read. Tail then settled into a 20-24% range and has printed 20% for the last thirteen hours. Stress climbed from 73% to a 79% peak as the long-end yield selloff intensified and held 78-79% overnight, while Confidence stayed at 87-89% throughout.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail at the watch floor through the early European hours while the unchanged overnight band contains price, steps it to 21-23% into the pre-release and release hours as depth thins, and reaches the 25% block threshold only conditionally for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots covering the U.S. cash open and the delayed-second-leg window after the payrolls print. That elevation is contingent on an aligned opening auction, shallow pullbacks and a long-end yield break back above 5.34%, not on the release itself. Stress peaks in the extreme band at 83% around the release and decays through the afternoon. From 21:00Z the weekend futures halt means no live price path can form, so the remaining slots hold the watch floor while Stress and Confidence step down to reflect a carried rather than observed assessment. The next live reference is the Sunday 22:00Z reopen and the next scheduled checkpoint is the ISM Services PMI on 5 October at 14:00Z.

forecastDetail.comment: NQ 30,874.25 sits inside an unchanged 30,760.25-30,934.75 overnight band after the marginal 30,934.75 high was rejected. With the 10-year flat at 5.240% and VIX at 16.39, the amplifier set is no longer aligned, so Tail holds the watch floor while Stress stays high on rates, the dollar and a weak Asian session.

European cash adds depth to the same narrow band. A break that holds would be the first genuine Tail trigger; a push that fades back inside would only reconfirm the two-sided structure already observed overnight.

Mid-morning Europe carries the overnight band forward by assumption. Long-end yields near 24-year peaks, a 17-month-high dollar and a partly unwound Gulf premium in Brent at 101.65 keep Stress high without implying a pathological path.
Tail steps to 21% as pre-release depth thins ahead of the 12:30Z payrolls print. Thinner liquidity raises the conditional cost of a band break but is not itself observed one-way structure.
Two hours before the release the mapped state stays in the watch band. A long-end yield push back above the 5.34% high would be the clearest conditional escalation marker for the hours that follow.

The final pre-release hour carries the least informative price path of the session, so Confidence eases to 87% while Stress reaches the extreme band at 80% on the overlap of near-record yields, a firm dollar and event proximity.
